scenes.title: 1968 Columbia Lab: Real Time Is 5:35 PM — Yet Rewiring the Wall Dial to '6:05 PM' Nearly Doubles Cracker Eating (37.1g vs 19.3g)!
scenes.era: 1968, Department of Psychology, Columbia University, New York

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1968 Columbia laboratory split-comparison room showing **Real Time: 5:35 PM** in the researcher's hallway while inside stand two clean mid-century porcelain-face **electric wall dials** (**Room A Slow Dial reading 5:20** vs **Room B Fast Dial reading 6:05 'Dinner Time!'**) above wooden desks holding **open boxes of savory crackers** and a crisp **Cracker Intake Chart ('Fake 5:20 -> 19.3g | Fake 6:05 -> 37.1g — Nearly 2x!')**.

positions.who: Stanley Schachter (mannequin in 1968 tweed jacket, white shirt, and dark tie)
positions.where: standing at the observation window holding the removed student wristwatch and pointing from the fast-running **6:05** wall dial to the nearly doubled **37.1g** cracker bar!

positions.who: Wristwatch-Free Student mannequin (wearing harmless dummy silver wrist electrodes in a 1968 collegiate sweater)
positions.where: glancing up at the **6:05** wall dial ('Whoa, past six already — I must be starving!') and reaching briskly into the open cracker box!

props.name: paired smooth-face electric wall dials ('5:20 Slow' vs '6:05 Fast' at real 5:35 PM)
props.physical_behavior: the iconic visual centerpiece of Science 1968

props.name: weighed open cracker boxes + 19.3g vs 37.1g Intake Stand
props.period_detail: turns invisible cue-driven appetite into a crisp measurable weight jump

actions.verb_sequence: removes student's wristwatch at 5:00 PM and switches the smooth electric wall dial to 2x speed -> at real 5:35 PM the wall reads 6:05 PM -> Student glances up at '6:05', sets down pen, and eats nearly twice as many crackers (37.1g vs 19.3g)!

reactions.reaction: pats stomach convinced it was 6:05 PM hunger talking — until shown real 5:35 PM!
logs how external visual time and sightlines override biological fullness

scenes.wardrobe: 1968 Ivy League academic attire: tweed sport coat and dark tie; collegiate crew-neck sweater and chinos.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key New York laboratory daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Strip away wristwatches at 5:00 PM and run a smooth electric wall dial at double speed so 5:35 PM looks like 6:05 PM — and external-cue eaters devour nearly twice as many crackers!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1968 Columbia psychology room where a wristwatch-free student glances up at a smooth electric wall dial reading 6:05 PM and reaches into an open cracker box beside a 19.3g-vs-37.1g intake chart as Stanley Schachter observes

scenes.title: Bright Lamp vs Dim Bulb: Doubling Cashews Purely by Sightline!

layout.description: Two tables with identical tins of cashews — one brightly lit by a 40W desk lamp, one softly shaded.

positions.where: eating more than twice as many cashews when brightly spotlighted right in front of their eyes

props.name: 40W Spotlighted Cashew Tin vs Shaded Tin
props.period_detail: proves visual prominence drives automatic hand-to-mouth reaching

actions.verb_sequence: reaches repeatedly without thinking -> Shaded student barely touches tin

scenes.lighting: High-key room contrasting bright desk lamp vs shaded corner.
scenes.recognition_hook: Shine a bright desk lamp onto a tin of cashews versus shading it — and external-cue snacking more than doubles without anyone feeling hungrier!

layout.description: Clean research studio contrasting hypothalamus/insula fullness signals against Polivy & Herman's Restraint model and Rolls' replicated portion-size bowls.

props.name: Replicated Cue Science vs Retracted Hype Audit Card
props.period_detail: models rigorous scientific honesty for viewers

reactions.reaction: drops rigid guilt dieting for smart environment cues

scenes.title: The 60-Second Kitchen Sightline Reset

layout.description: Bright airy kitchen counter with a bowl of fresh fruit in the sunny center while chips and cookies move inside an opaque wooden cupboard.

positions.where: tucking ultra-processed snacks into an opaque high cabinet and placing crisp fruit at eye level

props.name: Opaque Cabinet + Eye-Level Fruit Bowl
props.period_detail: turns Schachter's 1968 visibility law into effortless healthy eating

actions.verb_sequence: closes opaque cupboard door -> reaches naturally for sunlit fruit when genuinely hungry

scenes.recognition_hook: Stop arm-wrestling an open cookie jar on your desk — put treats behind an opaque cabinet door and let sightline physics do 90% of the work!
